summary_hint: <buydown_type> temporary buydown on loan <loan_number> (<lender_name>), <funding_party>-funded: note <note_rate>/<note_monthly_payment>, total subsidy <total_subsidy_amount>; <payment_schedule> reduced-payment periods.

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — the join key to the note / 1003 / CD; a buydown attaches to one specific loan
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the loan number VERBATIM as printed (it is masked at the snapshot boundary by the global PII registry — do not mask it here)

typed_core.name: lender_name
typed_core.why: identity — the party funding/administering the buydown subsidy account

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose payment is bought down; match to the borrower

typed_core.name: borrower_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — a co-borrower on a joint agreement
typed_core.prompt_hint: Only if a second borrower is named

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity — matches the subject property the buydown covers

typed_core.name: note_rate
typed_core.why: processor — the un-bought-down note rate; the baseline the schedule reduces FROM (the 'Interest Rate' column, constant across rows)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The permanent note rate, NOT the reduced first-year rate

typed_core.name: note_monthly_payment
typed_core.why: processor — the full note P&I; the qualifying-payment baseline (the borrower's ACTUAL outlay is reduced below this during the buydown period). NOTE: capture the fact; do NOT emit a 'qualifying payment' judgment (Priya / program call)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The full 'Total Monthly Payment' the note requires (= borrower payment + subsidy in any period)

typed_core.name: buydown_type
typed_core.why: processor — the structure label (2-1 / 1-0 / 3-2-1); a convenience descriptor, the payment_schedule is the source of truth
typed_core.prompt_hint: ONLY if explicitly labeled on the document (e.g. '2-1 Buydown'); if not stated, leave null — do NOT infer it from the schedule

typed_core.name: funding_party
typed_core.why: processor — who funds the subsidy (lender / seller / builder); bears on IPC / seller-concession limits
typed_core.prompt_hint: lender / seller / builder, from the 'LENDER PAID' / 'SELLER PAID' footer or the funding text, as stated

typed_core.name: total_subsidy_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the total buydown subsidy deposited into the account

typed_core.name: subsidy_account_holder
typed_core.why: processor — the named escrow/custodial holder of the subsidy account, when stated
typed_core.prompt_hint: The NAMED holder/custodian IF printed; many agreements say only 'a separate account for the benefit of the Borrower' — leave null then

typed_core.name: agreement_date
typed_core.why: processor — when the agreement was executed (recency / consistency with the note)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The 'EXECUTED THIS ... day of ...' date; if that line is blank, use the signature date

typed_core.name: is_signed
typed_core.why: processor — execution status; the borrower line is often blank at the disclosure stage
typed_core.prompt_hint: Who has signed: 'lender', 'borrower', 'both', or 'neither' (report what is actually signed)

nested_lists.name: payment_schedule
nested_lists.shape_reason: the substance of a buydown: a small per-PERIOD table (2 rows for a 2-1, 1 for a 1-0, 3 for a 3-2-1) of the reduced rate, the borrower's reduced payment, and the monthly subsidy applied. Small, so flat rows are cheap; one list keeps the type at the standard 8192 token tier.

fields.name: period_label
fields.why: the 'Payment Months' range label ('1-12', '13-24') — carries the period; there is no printed end DATE

fields.name: period_start
fields.why: the 'First Payment' date for the period (the period's start; the end is not printed)

fields.name: effective_rate
fields.why: the reduced (bought-down) interest rate for the period (4.125%, 5.125%)

fields.name: borrower_payment
fields.why: the 'Monthly Payment Paid by Borrower' — the reduced amount the borrower actually pays this period

fields.name: monthly_subsidy
fields.why: the 'Monthly Buydown Subsidy Application' — the subsidy that tops the borrower payment up to the note payment

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance — the row the values came from

rejected.name: payment_schedule.period_end
rejected.reason: NOT printed on the agreement — the schedule shows only the 'First Payment' (period start) and a 'Payment Months' range label. The label + start carry the period; a period-end date would be fabricated (LP-461 lesson).

rejected.name: qualifying_payment
rejected.reason: a JUDGMENT, not a fact — which payment qualifies the borrower (note vs bought-down vs a program-specific blend) is Priya's / the program's call. Tags describe; rules judge. Capture the schedule and rates; do not conclude the qualifying payment.

rejected.name: payment_schedule.total_monthly_payment (per row)
rejected.reason: the 'Total Monthly Payment' column equals note_monthly_payment on every row (borrower_payment + monthly_subsidy) — redundant with the scalar.

rejected.name: payment_schedule.note_interest_rate (per row)
rejected.reason: the per-row 'Interest Rate' column is the constant note rate — redundant with the note_rate scalar.

rejected.name: escrow_or_impound_terms
rejected.reason: the note/mortgage carry escrow; the buydown agreement only references them — catch-all

encoding_variations: buydown_type is frequently NOT labeled ('2-1' etc. may not appear); the schedule (rate deltas per period) is the true structure — degrade enum to str and leave null when unlabeled
funding_party appears as a 'LENDER PAID' / 'SELLER PAID' / 'BUILDER PAID' footer or in the funding sentence; the schedule shape is IDENTICAL across funding variants — only the funder differs
the schedule is PER-PERIOD (year ranges: '1-12', '13-24'), never per-month
the borrower's signature line is often blank at disclosure — is_signed must distinguish lender-only from fully executed
rates may print as '4.125%' or '4.125 %'; borrower payment sometimes shows the reduced rate in parentheses beside it

open_questions.q: buydown_type as a null-when-unlabeled scalar vs dropping it entirely
options: keep optional, null when the document does not label it
open_questions.recommendation: keep optional (GEET'S DECISION, LP-465): cheap and harmless, and some agreements DO print '2-1 Buydown' in the title; the schedule remains the source of truth when it is unlabeled
Decimal — a numeric rate is directly usable; the '%' is presentational

notes: loan_number is captured VERBATIM (full) here and masked at the snapshot boundary by the global _PII_FIELDS 'loan_number' registration (from_raw → masked display + a per-file match-hash, so it stays a usable cross-document join key). Do not pre-mask it in the prompt.

No judgment fields: no qualifying_payment, no DTI, no 'buydown compliant'. This type surfaces the buydown FACTS reliably (the ADR-465 rule: a processor needs it reliably even where no rule reads it yet) so a future qualifying-payment/DTI rule and the processor can both consume it.
The payment_schedule is the substance; the scalars are context. A 1-0 buydown yields one row, a 2-1 two, a 3-2-1 three.
